review.title: The Missing Eight
review.headline: A forgotten returned card framed an honest Owl and handed the cats the game.
review.summary: In Round 1, Drew was the only Meowfia, as the Sphinx. He gave himself away by changing his guess mid-sentence during a bluff, and five Farm players piled their cards on him. In Round 2, Ellis worked out Drew's starting nest size but forgot the S8 that came back to Drew after Round 1. That wrong math made the honest Owl Drew look like a liar. Drew got muddled too and attacked the honest Tit Ellis. The Farm split, and Ellis was eggsecuted 9 votes to 8. Finley, the Sphinx, won the game.

rounds.recap: Blair's Eagle report backed up Alex's and Finley's visits, so every Farm story checked out. Drew bluffed as the Tit and said 'guessed Hawk... no wait, Owl'. Finley really was the Hawk, so the slip looked like knowledge a cat would have. Drew was eggsecuted 27 votes to 0, and the Farm banked big scores.

Blair and Ellis first read nest sizes as changes since last round. Ellis then worked out Drew's baseline as 6 when it was really 7. That seemed to match Finley's fake Pigeon visit to Drew, so Drew's true 'unchanged' looked like a lie. Drew misread his Owl report as telling him who had visited him, called Ellis a liar, and threw 5 cards at him. With both cats also throwing at Ellis, the honest Tit was eggsecuted 9 to 8.

highlights.text: Drew's 'guessed Hawk... no wait, Owl' about the real Hawk sank his Tit bluff on the spot.
Finley's Sphinx knew which Farm roles were in play, so he quietly marked Alex's fake Hawk claim as a fellow cat (80% in his survey).
Ellis's careful baseline math missed Drew's returned S8, and that one error framed the only player telling the full truth.
The vote ended 9 to 8. The decider was Drew, an honest Farm player, throwing 5 cards at the honest Ellis.

confusions.what: His private reasoning said he would name Hawk with the Sphinx, but he named Eagle. Later he asked Blair to claim his role after Blair had already claimed Eagle.
Read the new nest sizes as egg gains and losses ('Alex and Finley lost eggs, Drew and Casey gained'), but nest sizes carry over between rounds.
Made the same mistake ('Drew +3, Finley -2, Alex -1'). His corrected baseline for Drew (4 kept + 2 drawn = 6) also missed the S8 returned to Drew in Round 1.
Repeated Ellis's wrong baseline of 6 for Drew and voted on it.
Claimed 'nobody visited me' and said Ellis 'never visited me'. His Owl report only covered Ellis's visitors, so he had no information about his own.
Private reasoning said 'visit Drew', but Casey's night choice was Ellis.

problems: Crimson Kunzea was revealed in both rounds, and nobody ever doubled down. You must commit before you have spoken, while the bonus only pays if you are right, so it never looks worth the risk. Let players double down later in the day, or give a reason to do it blind.

Nest sizes carry over between rounds, and the Round 1 consolation card changes them. Together these make it very hard to work out who gained eggs. That one math error decided Round 2. Have the Storyteller list each nest's size at the start of the night as well as at dawn.
The pool already held every animal at the start of Round 1, and the reveal turned up the same flower twice. So the per-round reveal added nothing. Check whether this is intended or a bug in the deck.
The log line 'Blair (Turkey) is hugged: no effect at tier 70' leaks engine debug text. It also shows that the Floofer's hug does nothing against a Turkey, which stays home and has no visit to cancel.

Throw sizes swing votes heavily. Drew's 7-card nest gave him the decisive 5 votes, while Finley threw everything in Round 1 and started Round 2 with only 2 cards. A round-one pile-on gives no-risk points (Casey banked 45). Round 2 was the only real contest.
